narrative:
The model predicts you have a 10% chance of failing your final year. While this is a low probability, it is high enough that the school requires you to take remedial courses as a precaution.

The prediction that you might fail is driven mainly by three aspects of your situation. The most influential factor is that you have had no past class failures. Surprisingly, this actually pushes the model toward expecting you to fail. Among students who passed, having zero previous failures is the average, yet in your specific combination of circumstances the model sees the complete lack of any prior academic struggle as a warning sign rather than a strength. 

The second most important influence is that you did not attend nursery school. This choice pulls the prediction toward passing, because most students who succeeded did attend nursery, so your background without it is less common among those who pass.

Third, your low amount of free time after school also nudges the outcome toward passing. Most students who passed reported medium or high free time, so your more limited free time is viewed as relatively positive by the model.

To improve, you should focus on building consistent study habits now, even with your low free time, and consider seeking extra academic support early. Strengthening these areas can reduce your risk and help you succeed without needing the remedial courses later. (218 words)
